title: Frequency comb generation in active optomechanical cavities
abstract: We numerically investigate frequency-comb generation in an electrically pumped vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser coupled to two mechanical modes of a suspended mirror. Displacement-dependent cavity loss and radiation-pressure feedback couple the mechanical motion to the carrier and photon densities, producing harmonics and combination-frequency components in the photon-density spectrum. Mechanical quality factors primarily control the intensity of comb lines, whereas resonance frequencies determine their spectral distribution. The initial mechanical amplitudes influence the threshold current and relative spectral intensities, with the simultaneous excitation of both modes yielding a broader set of observable components. These results establish the dependence of the calculated comb structure on mechanical dissipation, resonance frequencies, and initial conditions in an active optomechanical cavity.
summary: This paper numerically models frequency comb generation in an active optomechanical cavity formed by a VCSEL coupled to a MEMS mirror. By analyzing the coupled dynamics, the authors demonstrate that the resulting optical spectrum is a comb whose detailed structure is governed by the mechanical damping, resonance frequencies, and initial excitation levels. This work is significant for understanding controlled, nonlinear light sources in integrated quantum optics platforms.
main_problem: The paper investigates the generation of optical frequency combs in an active optomechanical cavity system.
main_result: The system self-sustainably generates a frequency comb whose structure is highly dependent on mechanical dissipation, resonance frequencies, and initial excitation amplitudes.
method: The study uses numerical simulations to solve coupled rate equations describing mechanical motion, carrier density, and photon density.
model_or_system: The physical system is an electrically pumped VCSEL coupled to two mechanical modes of a suspended MEMS mirror. The dynamics are modeled by coupling the mechanical oscillators to the cavity photon and carrier dynamics via radiation-pressure feedback.
key_observables: Frequency-comb structure in the photon-density spectrum, threshold current ($I_{th}$), and relative spectral intensities of comb lines.
important_parameters: Mechanical quality factors ($Q_j$), mechanical resonance frequencies ($f_j$), and initial mechanical amplitudes ($A_j(0)$).
main_assumptions: The model neglects direct elastic and photothermal coupling, and the calculated spectrum is for the intracavity intensity variable, requiring phase-resolved calculation for full field coherence.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device structure, the time and spectrum of the comb in photon density, and the dependence of the comb structure and threshold current on varying quality factors, resonance frequencies, and initial amplitudes.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the coupled dynamical model, analyzes the spectral components arising from nonlinear cavity response, and systematically investigates how varying mechanical parameters (dissipation, frequency, initial amplitude) controls the resulting comb structure and the system's operating threshold.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses nonlinear cavity dynamics and optomechanical coupling, which are central themes in cavity QED and open quantum systems. The detailed mapping of spectral features to mechanical parameters provides a rich platform for understanding quantum light sources.
